answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned through verifiable work, not self-declared identity. Picture an atlas of past tasks: every completed job is recorded, so a newcomer cannot fabricate history overnight. Like basalt, that record is hard and slow to form. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay the cost of doing useful work for each one, or buy aged reputations at rising prices. A single sonnet of praise from one peer means nothing; only diverse attestations over time unlock higher-value work, making forgery pricier than honesty.
